mainEntity.name: What is the Ontario Addiction Treatment Centre (OATC)?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Ontario Addiction Treatment Centre (OATC) is a rehabilitation center in Ontario that was founded in 1995 to provide opioid agonist therapy using methadone to people struggling with addiction.

mainEntity.name: What types of therapies are offered at OATC?

acceptedAnswer.text: OATC offers a wide range of therapies, including 1-on-1 counseling, art therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, physiotherapy, relapse prevention counseling, and yoga.

OATC’s treatment philosophy is holistic, medical, personalized, and wellness-oriented. The center’s staff believes that each patient is unique and requires an individualized treatment plan to achieve long-term recovery.
OATC treats a variety of conditions, including alcohol addiction, anxiety, cocaine addiction, heroin addiction, sex addiction, and more.

mainEntity.name: What aftercare services does OATC offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: OATC offers aftercare services such as family follow-up counseling, in-person follow-up sessions, and support meetings to help patients maintain their sobriety after leaving the facility.
OATC provides amenities such as air-conditioned rooms, fitness centers, gardens, and outdoor spaces to ensure that patients are comfortable during their stay.

mainEntity.name: What is the success rate of Ontario Addiction Treatment Centre?

acceptedAnswer.text: Success rates for addiction treatment can vary depending on the individual and their unique circumstances. However, OATC is committed to providing comprehensive treatment plans and aftercare services to help patients achieve long-term sobriety.

mainEntity.name: Can family members visit patients at Ontario Addiction Treatment Centre?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members can visit patients at OATC during designated visiting hours. The center also offers family follow-up counseling to help loved ones understand addiction and support their family member’s recovery.

mainEntity.name: How long does treatment at Ontario Addiction Treatment Centre last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treatment plans at OATC are personalized and may vary in length depending on the patient’s needs. However, the center typically offers 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day programs.

sections.heading: Ontario Addiction Treatment Centres - Center Overview

blocks.text: The Ontario Addiction Treatment Centres (OATC) were established in 1995 to provide much-needed opioid agonist therapy using methadone as treatment was severely limited. Today, OATC offers its services to over 50 communities across Ontario, treating over 10,000 patients daily with a focus on encouraging long-term sobriety from all illicit substances. The center’s staff is dedicated to providing optimal care, with a harm reduction approach that acknowledges drug addiction’s harmful outcomes, including victimization, overdose, and incarceration, among others. In addition to opioid addiction, OATC also offers therapy to address other addictive substances such as nicotine, cocaine, alcohol, and marijuana, as well as medical consequences such as Hepatitis C and HIV care.

With a focus on personalized treatment, harm reduction, and aftercare services, OATC remains committed to helping individuals achieve long-term recovery and a healthier lifestyle.
